biography.plain_text: Augustus James Newman was a British industrialist and chairman and managing director of Newman Industries, the electric-motor manufacturer based in Yate. He worked in the business alongside his father, Stephen, and brother, Hedley. Appointed a CBE in 1964, he later shared an international life with his wife, Frances Moody Newman.

biography.html: Augustus James Newman was a British industrialist and chairman and managing director of Newman Industries, the electric-motor manufacturer based in Yate. He worked in the business alongside his father, Stephen, and brother, Hedley. Appointed a CBE in 1964, he later shared an international life with his wife, Frances Moody Newman.

long_biography.plain_text:
At Lawns House in Yate, industrialist Augustus Newman made room for Belgian refugees during the Second World War. The house belonged to him from the 1940s and remained his home into the 1960s. His connection with the town extended to the former aircraft-repair works that became the base for his family's engineering business.

The company adapted its manufacturing to new markets after the war. It briefly produced compact tractors for small farms and developed specialised electric motors for pumps and other industrial equipment. By adapting fan motors to revised American standards, it also established export business in the United States.

confidence.reason: Heritage Centre map directly attributes refugee accommodation to Newman; county history corroborates the works. Industrial history documents company products and US standards adaptation. No personal invention or sole responsibility for company decisions is asserted.
